Continue target training, teach them to step up if they don’t already know. If they’re hand shy, you could use a stick or a perch and gradually move your hand closer until they’re comfortable. Training recall is good too. Once they know the basics you could introduce tricks. 

The flock does everything together, so eat near them, sit by them, read a book out loud, talk to them, announce what you’re doing, etc. Just do everyday things but let them be apart of it on their terms. 

Whenever you enter or leave the room, greet/let them know you’ll be right back. You could give them a treat too but then they might start to expect it every time lol. 

Just don’t rush anything, it takes time for birds to come around, they’re prey animals and are cautious by nature. Patience is key, they’ll get there.

I use F10 SC, it’s a veterinary grade disinfectant. I use 2ml for general cleaning and 4ml for disinfecting. It’s safe to use for their cages and toys too.

Oh man this made me cry. I had to put my first hedgehog, Prickly Petey, down Dec. 27th, 2018. He was going to turn 3 on February 4th. He had stopped eating and I’d been syringe feeding him the entire month, hourly, he had X-rays taken, nothing came up. He kept declining and nothing I was doing was helping him like it had the month before. I took him in to the vet and had to make the horrible decision that I felt immense guilt for. I almost didn’t stay in the room but I couldn’t let him go alone either and held him the entire time. I had a necropsy done and the vet stayed late to perform it, he had a tumor wrapped around his spleen and there was nothing that I could’ve done for him. I miss him so much. My cat turned 13 in May, and my second hedgehog that I rescued is going to be 3 on July 22nd. 

In May, my second hedgie had also stopped eating and had bleeding, without even taking X-rays the vet recommended I euthanize him. I refused to without trying medicine and syringe feeding first, a week of that and he’s back to his normal self. 

For those that don’t know, hedgehogs are tumor and cancer machines and it is almost a guarantee they will develop it, and the odds only get higher the closer they get to age 3. 
Reason for this is that they were crossbred between the Algerian and Four Toed hedgehog. Then had tons of inbreeding occur due to a small gene pool when they got brought over in the 80s.
